header.div: ZPMS · plan for approval · revised after three design rounds
header.h1: Clinical tags in the note boxes
header.p: While writing an ordinary note, you mark clinical facts inline with a short Greek tag such as @δγ or @επ. The prose stays readable and unbroken. ZPMS stores each tagged value separately, so the patient record can show diagnoses, levels, allergies, the plan and medication at a glance, and you can search by them.

tr.td: Inside the sentence, no chips or boxes. The tag word itself is faint grey.
The sentence holding the caret gets a pale wash per field. Finished sentences keep only a very pale, thin underline.
Tag words hidden, each value in a soft tinted ink. Tagged allergies also on the patient header.

Ghost completion everywhere, Tab one word at a time, never the whole suggestion by default; → takes the rest. On a phone, the suggestion shows as word buttons above the keyboard. ↓ opens the full list; checklists for exams and levels; fill-in blanks for prescriptions; next-word strip after exams, physiotherapy and therapies.
Nine (table below). @αγ (recommended treatment) stays separate from @συν (prescribed today).
Greek short tags and Greek lists, so the keyboard never changes. English tags still work. Levels accepted in Greek and English notation.
A basic Greek starter list per field, growing from your previous entries.
Appointment notes and the patient note (confirmed). The home-page notes are personal and not about one patient, so no tags there.
Five parts in one phrase: drug, strength (mg), doses per day, days, optional short note.

section.div: Προτείνεται @εξ μαγνητική τομογραφία ΟΜΣΣ, στο @επ Ο4-Ο5 με πίεση της ρίζας.

ul.li: Start: @ followed by a known tag name, at the start of the text or after a space or punctuation. An email address or a lone @ is never taken as a tag.
End: the value ends at the next comma, semicolon (Greek «·» or «;»), line break, another tag, or a full stop followed by a space. A full stop inside a number (0.5mg) ends nothing.
Per field: a level value ends by itself after its last level, so «στο @επ Ο4-Ο5 με πίεση» takes only «Ο4-Ο5». A prescription may contain commas and ends at a semicolon, full stop or line break.
Matching: tag names and list searches ignore capitals and Greek accents (@ΔΙΑΓΝΩΣΗ, @διαγνωση and @δγ are the same).

tr.td: Κήλη μεσοσπονδυλίου δίσκου, Δισκοπάθεια, Σπονδυλική στένωση, Σπονδυλολίσθηση, Ριζοπάθεια, Αυχενική μυελοπάθεια, Μηνιγγίωμα, Γλοίωμα, Υδροκέφαλος, Σύνδρομο καρπιαίου σωλήνα
Built in: Α1–Α7, Θ1–Θ12, Ο1–Ο5, Ι1 (C, T, L, S)
Πενικιλλίνη, ΜΣΑΦ, Ασπιρίνη, Ιωδιούχα σκιαγραφικά, Λάτεξ, Καμία γνωστή αλλεργία
Μαγνητική τομογραφία, Αξονική τομογραφία, Ηλεκτρομυογράφημα, Ακτινογραφία, Δυναμική ακτινογραφία, Σπινθηρογράφημα οστών, Αιματολογικός έλεγχος
Μικροδισκεκτομή, Πεταλεκτομή, Αποσυμπίεση, Σπονδυλοδεσία, Πρόσθια αυχενική δισκεκτομή και σπονδυλοδεσία, Τρηματοτομή, Απελευθέρωση καρπιαίου σωλήνα, Κρανιοτομία
Επισκληρίδιος έγχυση, Ριζική διήθηση, Διήθηση facet, Ραδιοσυχνότητες, Κηδεμόνας, Αυχενικό κολάρο
Φυσικοθεραπεία ΟΜΣΣ, Φυσικοθεραπεία ΑΜΣΣ, Ασκήσεις σταθεροποίησης κορμού, Κινησιοθεραπεία, Υδροθεραπεία
ΜΣΑΦ επί πόνου, Παρακεταμόλη επί πόνου, Μυοχαλαρωτικό, Πρεγκαμπαλίνη, Γκαμπαπεντίνη, Κορτικοστεροειδή σε σχήμα, Γαστροπροστασία
Lyrica, Neurontin, Depon, Apotel, Mydocalm, Medrol, each with its usual doses. Names written as on the box, found by Greek spelling (λυρ finds Lyrica).

section.p: Field names, tags and colours live in one place in the code, so adding a tenth field later is a small change.
Tags are not hand-coded one by one. Two layers:

ul.li: Value types (code, few): text (ends at a comma, «·»/«;», full stop or line break), levels (ends by itself, Greek or English, normalised), prescription (five parts, may contain commas). Each one has its parser, picker and tests.

Tag definitions (one file in the app's config, no code): per tag an internal key, label, names (the first is the main short tag; all are accepted), colour, value type, picker (list, checklist, grid, blanks), and flags for next words, the summary panel, the patients-list filter and the patient-header alert.

section.div: dx: label: Διάγνωση names: [δγ, διάγνωση, dx, diagnosis] colour: rose value: text picker: list summary: true search: true

ul.li: The parser, menus, colours, summary panel, search filters and the Settings list page all read this one definition.

Adding a tag of an existing type is a new entry plus its starter list, with no code. A new value type (e.g. a follow-up period @επαν 3 μήνες, or a score @vas 7/10) needs code and tests once; every later tag of that type is free.

Safe for old notes: note_fields stores the internal key (dx), never the typed name, so labels and colours can change freely. Names are only ever added, never removed, so «@δγ» in an old note is always recognised. After a definition change the rebuild command re-reads all notes.
The definition lives in a config file, changed through a normal update. A Settings page for adding tags yourself can come later if needed. The list entries themselves are already edited in Settings.

section.p: Accepted in either notation, mixed, any case, with a dash, slash or the short form: Ο4-Ο5, ο4-5, Ο4/Ο5, L4-L5, l4-5, Ο5-Ι1, Α5-Α6, Θ12. Α = αυχενική (C), Θ = θωρακική (T), Ο = οσφυϊκή (L), Ι = ιερό (S).

ul.li: The note keeps exactly what you typed.
ZPMS also stores a normalised English form (L4-L5), so a search or the summary finds the level however it was written.
An impossible level (Ο6, Α9) is kept as typed, shown with a quiet warning, and left out of the summary. A save is never refused.

section.p: Written as one readable phrase: Lyrica 75mg 1x2 για 30 ημέρες, μετά το φαγητό.

tr.td: The drug list, found by Greek spelling
First word(s), matched to the list
A number with mg (also μγ, mcg, g, ml)
μετά το φαγητό, πριν το φαγητό, πριν τον ύπνο, με σταδιακή αύξηση, plus your own
Whatever follows the comma; anything not placed elsewhere

ul.li: A prescription value may contain commas and ends at a semicolon (Greek «·» or «;»), full stop or line break, so two drugs in one sentence are separated with «·».
The total number of doses (doses per day × days, e.g. 2 × 30 = 60) is shown in the bar while writing and in the summary when it can be worked out.
Prescriptions are a record for the notes; there is no connection to e-prescribing.

ol.li: Fixed list for the field: the starter entries plus anything promoted in Settings. Shown first, marked as list wording.
Your previous entries for that field across all notes, most used first, with a count.
Next words per list entry (after «μαγνητική τομογραφία»: ΟΜΣΣ, ΑΜΣΣ, ΘΜΣΣ, εγκεφάλου…), plus words you have written after that entry before.

ul.li: Ghost completion (default): the best match appears in grey after the caret. Tab takes the next word only; press again for the next. → at the end of the text takes the rest at once. Typing anything else ignores it. On a phone (no Tab or arrow keys) the suggestion shows as buttons above the keyboard, one per word: a tap takes the suggestion up to that word, «✓ όλο» takes it all, and tapping the grey ghost text does the same.
Full list: ↓ opens it, Enter picks, Esc closes.
Checklist: for exams and levels, tick several; Enter writes them into the sentence as text («Ο3-Ο4 και Ο4-Ο5»).
Fill-in blanks: a prescription entry brings blanks for strength, doses per day, days and a short note, each with its own short list; Tab (or «επόμενο ›» on a phone) moves between blanks.
Next-word strip: after an exam, physiotherapy or therapy entry; a number key or click inserts the word.
↑ ↓ move the highlight in every menu; in the level grid ← → move along the row.
Space ticks or unticks the highlighted item in checklists and the level grid. In single-choice lists and blanks Space keeps typing, because entries contain spaces.
Enter accepts: the highlighted entry in a list, every ticked item in a checklist or grid, the blank's value (then moves to the next blank).
Esc closes without changing anything. Clicks and taps do the same as Space and Enter.

section.p: A new admin page under Settings, «Λίστες σημειώσεων», in the same style as Clinics and Doctors: per field, add, edit, reorder or remove entries; set next words and prescription blanks; see your most frequent free-text entries that are not yet on the list, with a one-click «add to list».
A click or tap puts the caret exactly where you clicked, as in any text box; nothing pops up over the words. When the caret is inside a tagged value:

ul.li: its sentence takes the writing wash and a thin dashed frame marks the value's exact words;
a slim bar at the top of the note box (above the keyboard on a phone) names the field and offers: list (↓), change field, remove tag.
Typing inside the value changes it; the frame follows by the same ending rules as when writing.
From the list, Enter replaces the whole value inside the frame, with the current value shown first.
Levels reopen the grid with the current levels selected; clicks add or remove.
Prescriptions written from a list entry get their blanks back (strength, doses per day, days, note) when the caret enters one.
Wrong field: clicking the grey tag word opens the tag menu; the value stays and only the field and colour change.
Remove the tag, keep the words: one Backspace right after a tag word deletes the whole tag word, or use «αφαίρεση ετικέτας» from the bar.
From the reading view: a click opens the card for writing with the caret on the clicked word; read-only accounts get no change.
The note text is the truth. It is saved exactly as typed, in the same columns as today (appointments.anote, patients.pnote). Old notes need no conversion.

note_fields: one row per tagged value, rebuilt for that note on every save: patient, source (appointment or patient note), field, value as typed, normalised value, valid or not, position in the text. A one-off command fills it from existing notes and can rebuild it at any time.
note_list_entries: the fixed lists: field, text, search aliases (Greek spelling of drug names), next words, prescription blanks, order, active. Seeded with the starter lists.
For prescriptions, note_fields also keeps the parts separately: drug, strength (mg), doses per day as written (1x2) and as a number, days, note, and the total doses when they can be worked out.
Previous entries and their counts are read from note_fields, so nothing extra has to be kept in step.

section.p: One set of rules written twice: PHP for saving and reading, JavaScript for the live colours and suggestions. Both run the same shared list of test cases, so they can't drift. The tags, their names and their colours come from one definition the server sends to the page.

ul.li: Stays a plain text box, so autosave, copy and paste and mobile keyboards work as today.

A coloured copy of the text is drawn exactly behind it in the same font, and the box's own letters are made transparent. The washes and underlines live in that copy; nothing in it takes space, so the letters never move.
The ghost text, menus, checklist and blanks are small hand-written scripts (no new library), the same family as the patient-name search.
Read-only notes are rendered by PHP with the tag words removed and values in tinted ink, every piece escaped as today.
The patient header gets an allergy line. A «Κλινική εικόνα» panel lists each field's entries with their date and a link to the note they came from.

section.p: The patients list gets filters for diagnosis, level and procedure, matched against note_fields (normalised levels, accent-insensitive text).

The values are patient data and follow the notes' rules: never written to the audit log (only the event and field names), deleted with the patient when a record is purged, and shown only to accounts that can already see that patient. Suggestions only come from notes the signed-in user is allowed to read.

ol.li: Rules and storage. The parser in PHP and JavaScript with shared tests; note_fields and note_list_entries with the Greek starter lists; extraction on every save; the rebuild command.
Writing. The coloured copy behind the box: the wash on the current sentence, the pale underline elsewhere. The @ tag menu.
Suggestions and editing. Ghost completion word by word, the full list on ↓, checklists, prescription blanks and the next-word strip; the value frame and the field bar for editing.
Reading. The clean read-only view, the allergy line and the «Κλινική εικόνα» panel.
Lists and search. The «Λίστες σημειώσεων» Settings page and the patients-list filters.

section.p: Each phase is usable on its own and comes with its own tests in the existing suite. Phases 1 and 2 together already give tagged, coloured notes; the rest adds speed and payoff.

div.p: All points are settled: → takes the rest of a suggestion (word buttons on a phone), tags work in appointment notes and the patient note, and prescriptions have five parts. On approval, work starts with phase 1, the rules and storage.
